digest:
Part A — Case digest

Client/matter: Justin W. Sapini, DOB 12/21/1995. Current listed address is 20510 Cypress Plaza Parkway, Apt. 3211, Cypress, TX 77433; prior NY address at accident/intake was 7 Valley Drive, Nanuet, NY 10954. Defendants are Anthony F. Ferrara and Metro-North Commuter Railroad. Claim administered by Claims Service Bureau, claim SIR068120. Action: Supreme Court, New York County, Index No. 160000/2024. Judge shown in correspondence: Hon. Christopher Chin.

Incident story and posture: DOI 04/23/2023 at about 8:30 a.m. on Cedar Street at/near Garden Street, New Rochelle, Westchester County, NY, immediately adjacent to a Metro-North facility. Plaintiff was driving a 2012 Volkswagen GLI, NY plate KYR1393. Adverse vehicle was a 2019 Chevrolet utility vehicle, PA plate ZMP3277, Metro-North unit E2858D, with Metro-North badging and “We Aim High to Drive Safe”/1-800-773-1753 markings, operated by Anthony F. Ferrara. No ambulance; client drove himself home and went to Montefiore Nyack Hospital the next day, 04/24/2023. The complaint pleads Ferrara was in the course of employment, pulling into a Metro-North facility, but also pleads in the alternative that Ferrara was not working and was on a break. The Metro-North IR-1/incident report identifies Ferrara as Assistant Foreman, MoW C&S, employee no. 115290, and checks “On-Duty,” with incident description that Ferrara was heading to the jobsite and was sideswiped by another vehicle at I-95 Southbound Exit 16/New Rochelle. That is favorable on scope but not fully resolved because assignment/dispatch records remain outstanding and defendants have not cleanly admitted scope in discovery.

Liability/risk: Liability is contested on two levels. First, mechanism. The plaintiff-side file identifies three inconsistent accounts from/attributable to client: (1) Metro-North vehicle merged into his lane and struck him; (2) both vehicles were merging and his vehicle struck the other; (3) sideswiped by a truck and struck the sidewalk. Pleadings/BOP adopt that defendants negligently merged into plaintiff’s lane; BOP says both vehicles were southbound and defendant’s passenger-side door contacted plaintiff’s driver-side door/front fender. Defense incident report says Ferrara/Metro-North was sideswiped by another vehicle on passenger side. There is no reliable presumption of fault on a sideswipe/merging-lanes case. A police accident report is referenced in plaintiff’s discovery response and IME record review, but internal notes repeatedly state no police report had been obtained; this is a contradiction needing file audit. Client said on 05/07/2023 he had 22 scene photos; plaintiff’s 01/02/2025 discovery response says plaintiff has 22 color copied photos of property damage/injuries, but internal notes say none were obtained earlier. Defendants produced five vehicle photographs. Second, scope of employment. Metro-North’s own IR-1 says on-duty and heading to jobsite; nonetheless defense has resisted vehicle assignment/dispatch records as overbroad, and counsel/adjuster would not take a position on 05/24/2025. Kyle Pullano is listed in defendants’ response as a Metro-North employee/passenger in the defendant vehicle and is the person identified as able to answer scope. A subpoena for his virtual EBT was filed 11/02/2025 for 12/08/2025, but notes as late as 03/06/2026 and 09/15/2026 still list Pullano deposition/scope disclosure outstanding.

Injuries/treatment: Initial ER at Montefiore Nyack on 04/24/2023 for neck, upper back, left shoulder pain and lightheadedness. CT head negative; CT cervical negative for acute fracture. Treaters include Advanced Rockland Chiropractic/Kevin Haggerty, D.C.; Interventional PM&R/Vadim Abramov, M.D.; McCulloch Orthopaedic/Dr. David Capiola and Nicole Kosuda, P.A.; SportsCare PT/Michael Ludena, P.T.; Hudson Valley Radiology/Mid Rockland; New Horizon Surgical Center; Dr. Peter C. Kwan neurology; Dr. Melinda L. Miller EMG/NCV. Claimed injuries in BOP: left shoulder labral/infraspinatus tears with surgery, right shoulder rotator cuff/labral/infraspinatus tears with need for arthroscopy, left wrist sprain/strain, right hand tingling, head/TBI/post-concussion findings, bilateral knee meniscal tears/edema, cervical C5-6 bulge/straightening, lumbar L5-S1 bulge, thoracic myofascial derangement. Chiropractic began 04/26/2023, intensive 3x/week until 11/21/2023, then weekly through at least 08/15/2024 records and reportedly continuing. PT began 06/29/2023 and records through 12/14/2023, but chart oddity: discharge note dated 09/14/2023 followed by continued daily PT notes through 12/14/2023. As of 2025–2026 client reports ongoing PT/chiro weekly or twice weekly, no discharge, no MMI, tramadol and ibuprofen PRN.

Imaging/procedures: MRIs through Hudson Valley/Mid Rockland: cervical and lumbar on 05/08/2023; bilateral shoulders on 05/24/2023; bilateral knees on 07/03/2023; brain MRI/DTI/volumetrics on 08/08/2023. Cervical: straightening lordosis, shallow C5-6 bulge flattening left ventral canal margin. Lumbar: L5-S1 bulge with lateral predominance narrowing lateral recesses/inferior foramina bilaterally. Left shoulder: posterior inferior labral tear at 8–9 o’clock, low-grade posterior infraspinatus interstitial tear, inferior glenohumeral ligament thickening, and hypoplasia of posterior inferior glenoid/developmental glenoid rim deficiency. Right shoulder: intermediate-grade anterior infraspinatus interstitial tear and partial posterior inferior labral tear at 8 o’clock. Knees: plaintiff radiology says posterior horn medial meniscus tears bilaterally and left prepatellar edema. Brain MRI/DTI: treating radiology says 2/12 ROIs and 1/6 white matter tracts abnormal, hemosiderin focus right parietal gray-white junction, PPV for TBI >95%; defense radiology disputes this.

Left shoulder surgery: 07/26/2023 at New Horizon Surgical Center, Paterson, NJ, by Dr. David Capiola. Procedure: left shoulder exam under anesthesia and arthroscopy, posterior labral repair using 2.99 mm BioComposite PushLock anchor/cinch stitch, complete synovectomy, lysis of adhesions, subacromial decompression, extensive debridement of biceps tendon, partial rotator cuff tear, and cartilage defect. Post-op diagnosis: significant posterior labral tear, synovitis, adhesions, impingement, partial biceps tendon tear, partial rotator cuff tear, cartilage defect.

Right shoulder surgery: Dr. Capiola recommended right shoulder arthroscopy on 05/27/2024 and repeated recommendation on 10/24/2025; still not performed or scheduled. Multiple chasers to McCulloch/Capiola: 05/05/2026, 06/14/2026 call, 07/04/2026, 08/03/2026, 09/17/2026. On 09/24/2026 McCulloch said Dr. Capiola wants to see client again before scheduling and no date can be given. Client previously deferred because he could not afford to be out of work again; later says willing to proceed. This is the major valuation hold.

Money/value/coverage: Estimated case value field and 06/04/2026 evaluation: $375,000. Economics alone stated as $332,400 = $118,400 specials + $214,000 wage loss, with second shoulder surgery still recommended. Practical recovery is capped at defendant BI limits unless another coverage/defendant theory changes. Coverage history is internally inconsistent: early notes say Metro-North is self-insured/no declarations/no ceiling and Ferrara personal auto $100k/$300k if Metro-North exits. Later Claims Service Bureau emails dated 09/08/2026 confirm BI limits $100,000 per person/$300,000 per occurrence, no excess/umbrella; field says coverage confirmed true. Client UM/UIM is $25,000/$50,000, below defendant limits and adds nothing. No-fault through Progressive: $50,000 basic economic loss, exhausted per 12/19/2023 and 01/10/2025 emails; under Insurance Law 5104(a), exhausted no-fault not recoverable from tortfeasor. Medicaid lien asserted at $22,180 as of 03/28/2024; reaffirmed unchanged 07/23/2025. SSD claim filed and pending; defendants pleaded CPLR 4545 collateral source.

Specials: Working/interim medical specials total $118,400 across nine providers: New Horizon Surgical Center facility/anesthesia $60,000; Hudson Valley Radiology/Mid Rockland seven MRI studies $15,900; Advanced Rockland Chiropractic $14,220; McCulloch/Dr. Capiola including surgeon fee $9,530; SportsCare PT $5,825; Dr. Miller EMG/NCV $4,800; Montefiore Nyack ER/CTs $3,475; Dr. Kwan neurology $3,200; Abramov physiatry $1,450. Payment status unknown on bills. Specials are not final because chiropractic and PT ledgers are open/ongoing and not reconciled line-by-line against CPT codes.

Wage loss: $214,000 claimed. Client is/was a Northwestern Mutual financial advisor, commission-only, at 875 Third Avenue, New York, NY 10022. Out of work since DOI and continuing per BOP/notes. Claim currently rests on client’s 2022 1099 only; no economic expert retained and no later commission/production records despite repeated requests. Defendants attacked wage claim as unsupported by expert. Pending task to obtain updated employment/commission records was due 09/26/2026; client said on 09/27/2026 he would send them “soon.”

Demand/negotiations: Demand package served 04/12/2024 to Claims Service Bureau with specials $118,400, wage loss $214,000, left shoulder surgery, TBI findings, Medicaid lien and exhausted no-fault disclosed; chiro/PT ledgers marked subject to revision. Adjuster response 04/29/2024: negotiations opened with offer well under defendant’s $100,000 limit; position was liability contested on mechanism, day-after CTs clean, wage claim unsupported by expert. No counter served; file note says do not settle while treatment open and ledgers unreconciled. Later right shoulder surgery recommendation overtook demand.

Litigation/procedure: Prior lawsuit began 02/01/2024 but was dismissed for failure to satisfy Public Authorities Law §1276 presentation-of-claim prerequisite before suit. New complaint filed under CPLR 205 after overnight Presentation of Claim served 09/10/2024 and 30 days elapsed. Current summons/complaint filed NY County; document page shows filed 10/11/2024, complaint dated 10/15/2024 and verification 10/29/2024 — internal document metadata says received 03/08/2024, which conflicts with pleading pages. Court filing expense entry says 07/21/2024 for index 160000/2024, another date inconsistency. Defendants answered 12/02/2024. BOP served/filed 01/02/2025. Letter to Judge Chin dated 04/16/2025 requested PC/case scheduling order after RJI/PC request filed 01/02/2025 and no date received. Limitations task due 04/22/2026 says SOL satisfied by notice/presentation and suit commenced within time.

Defense experts: Orthopedic IME by Dr. Emmanuel Hostin occurred per report on 03/31/2026, served 04/09/2026, although file events also list 09/02/2026 IME attendance and 09/14/2026 service; this is a date contradiction. Hostin recorded client refused to provide general past medical history, had subjective complaints not correlating with objective/radiographic findings, found conditions medically stationary/plateaued, diagnosed resolved neck/mid-back/low-back/bilateral shoulder/elbow/knee/wrist sprains, and said plaintiff can return to work without restrictions. He noted guarding, inconsistent lumbar ROM behavior, no objective spasm/contracture/bony derangement, and positive left cubital tunnel Tinel without indicated treatment. Neurology expert Dr. Jack W. Tsao report dated 03/04/2026 and served 03/24/2026, but file events also discuss neurological IME 09/07/2026 and report served later; date contradiction. Tsao found normal neuro exam/cervical and lumbar ROM, diagnosed status post post-concussion syndrome/headaches/TBI/cervical/thoracic/lumbar strain objectively resolved, incidental bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, and ability to work/ADLs without restrictions. Defense radiologist Dr. Marc J. Katzman report dated 12/08/2025, exchanged 02/04/2026, disputes plaintiff imaging: right and left knees normal/no traumatic injury/internal derangement; right shoulder unremarkable/no traumatic injury; chest x-ray 2018 no acute findings; brain MRI/DTI/NeuroQuant normal/no traumatic brain injury, with footnote attacking individual clinical use of advanced neuroimaging.

Overdue/upcoming/holders: Pending/overdue tasks as of current file date 10/02/2026 include McCulloch updated records/right shoulder surgical date due 08/25/2026 (holder: McCulloch/Capiola; Matthew assigned), updated employment and commission records due 09/26/2026 (holder: client; Matthew assigned), reconcile chiropractic and PT ledgers due 10/05/2026 (holder partly Advanced Rockland/SportsCare, then firm; Matthew assigned), Advanced Rockland current notes/itemized CPT bill due 10/07/2026 (holder: Advanced Rockland), confirm right shoulder arthroscopy date due 10/10/2026 (holder: McCulloch/Capiola), SportsCare ongoing treatment notes due 10/14/2026 (holder: SportsCare; two requests unanswered per task). Upcoming calendar: 10/09/2026 chiro session; 10/10/2026 PT session and call to McCulloch re surgery date; 10/14/2026 client follow-up on treatment/surgery/employment records; 10/17/2026 PT; 10/21/2026 file review on whether to move to compel assignment/dispatch records and how to value recommended-but-undated right shoulder surgery; 10/29/2026 client appointment to collect commission statements. Defense owes/holds vehicle assignment and dispatch records and full scope-of-employment disclosure; incident report status is contradictory because defendants’ 09/30/2025 response annexes an incident report, but 09/06/2026 note says incident report is still being searched for.

Last client contact: Last actual contact is 09/27/2026 call/note. Justin asked whether he should continue PT while case pending; advised yes and to keep his own record of each visit. He confirmed right shoulder surgery still has no date, said otherwise fine, and promised updated employment records “soon.” Upcoming client follow-up set for 10/14/2026; client appointment for employment records set 10/29/2026.

Contradictions/inconsistencies to resolve before deposition/settlement: (1) Mechanism: Metro-North merged into client vs both vehicles merging/client struck other vs sideswiped by truck and hit sidewalk; defense report says Metro-North/Ferrara was sideswiped by another vehicle. (2) Police report: internal notes say no police accident report obtained, but plaintiff discovery response says a Police Accident Report is annexed and IME records reviewed a police accident report dated 04/23/2023. (3) Scope: complaint pleads Ferrara in course of employment but also pleads alternative that he was on break/not working; Metro-North IR-1 checks on-duty and heading to jobsite, but scope disclosure/assignment records still not produced/accepted. (4) Coverage: early notes say Metro-North self-insured/no stated ceiling/no declaration; later confirmed BI limits $100k/$300k/no excess. (5) Prior injuries: client denied prior injuries, but file contains 10/05/2011 left ankle/foot x-rays showing small dorsal avulsion fracture of anterior talus and 09/10/2018 chest x-ray; he also reportedly complained of left ankle pain from this accident although no left ankle injury is pled/claimed. Hostin also lists left ankle among current accident injuries, but BOP does not plead ankle. (6) Treatment records: SportsCare discharge 09/14/2023 followed by treatment notes continuing through 12/14/2023. (7) PT/chiro current frequency: 2025 notes say weekly PT/chiro; 09/18/2026 note says PT twice weekly; calendars list weekly PT. (8) Right shoulder surgery: 07/09/2025 client said he had not scheduled/could not afford time off; later notes say willing to proceed; Hostin report says he reports scheduled for right shoulder arthroscopy in near future, while firm records say no date and McCulloch says no date. (9) IME dates: file calendar/tasks/notes put defense IMEs in September 2026, but defense reports are dated March 2026 and served March/April 2026; file also says “reports now served” 09/13/2026, inconsistent with document pages. (10) IME watchdog: 09/02/2026 note says watchdog attended both IMEs; 09/12/2026 client call says watchdog attended orthopedic one; Tsao report says watchdog was present at neuro. (11) Incident report production: defendants’ 09/30/2025 response annexes Metro-North incident report, yet 09/06/2026 note says incident report being searched for. (12) Pleading/file dates: complaint document metadata received 03/08/2024, but pleading pages show filed 10/11/2024/received 10/29/2024 and complaint dated 10/15/2024; court filing expense dated 07/21/2024; prior lawsuit timeline also involved February 2024. (13) Defense affirmative-defense BOP repeatedly misgenders plaintiff as “her/she.” (14) Plaintiff discovery response says “Plaintiff is not aware of witnesses other than parties and those listed on Police Accident Report,” but defendants later identify Kyle Pullano as passenger/witness. (15) BOP lists Lenox Hill Radiology as provider, while specials/imaging tally uses Hudson Valley/Mid Rockland for the brain MRI; Katzman review references Lenox Hill Radiology for brain imaging. (16) Address: client resides in Texas per pleadings/contact but continues treating in NY providers; need clarify travel/attendance logistics.

answers.answer: 04/23/2023 at about 8:30 a.m., on Cedar Street at/near Garden Street, New Rochelle, Westchester County, NY, adjacent to a Metro-North facility.
Estimated case value is $375,000.

Defendant BI limits are confirmed at $100,000 per person / $300,000 per occurrence, no excess/umbrella disclosed. Client UM/UIM is $25,000/$50,000 and adds nothing. Coverage is marked confirmed, though early notes described Metro-North as self-insured with no stated ceiling.
Medical specials to date are $118,400, interim/not final.
$214,000 wage loss claimed. It is supported only by client’s 2022 1099/commission-only Northwestern Mutual earnings; no economic expert and no later commission/production records yet.
Left shoulder arthroscopy was on 07/26/2023 at New Horizon Surgical Center, performed by Dr. David Capiola.

Right shoulder arthroscopy has been recommended since 05/27/2024 and repeated later, but remains unscheduled and unperformed. McCulloch/Capiola says Dr. Capiola wants to see client again before scheduling and no date can be given.
Yes. Progressive no-fault basic economic loss of $50,000 was exhausted.
Yes. New York State Medicaid lien is asserted at $22,180 and was unchanged as of the last lien note.
Three inconsistent accounts are noted.

Not finally admitted by defendants, but Metro-North’s IR-1 checks “On-Duty” and says Ferrara was heading to the jobsite. Scope remains a discovery issue because assignment/dispatch records and clear scope disclosure remain outstanding.

Kyle Pullano is a Metro-North employee/passenger in the defendant vehicle and the person identified as able to address scope of employment. He has not been substantively contacted/deposed per the latest notes, despite a subpoena filed for his EBT.
A 10/05/2011 left ankle/left foot injury: x-rays by Kenneth Blumberg, M.D. showing a small dorsal avulsion fracture of the anterior talus. Client denied prior injuries.

Dr. Emmanuel Hostin concluded the orthopedic conditions had plateaued/are medically stationary; neck, back, bilateral shoulder/elbow/knee/wrist sprains are resolved; subjective complaints/ROM limits do not correlate with objective findings; plaintiff can return to work without restrictions.

Dr. Jack W. Tsao concluded post-concussion syndrome, post-traumatic headaches/migraines, TBI, and cervical/thoracic/lumbar strains are objectively resolved; neuro exam was essentially normal; plaintiff can work and perform ADLs without restrictions.

Dr. Marc Katzman found no traumatic/internal derangement in either knee, right shoulder unremarkable/no traumatic injury, 2018 chest x-ray no acute findings, and brain MRI/DTI/NeuroQuant normal with no evidence of traumatic brain injury.

Last client contact was 09/27/2026. Justin called asking whether to continue PT; he was told yes and to keep his own visit log. He confirmed right shoulder surgery still had no date and said he would send updated employment records soon.

Overdue/pending items include: McCulloch updated records/right shoulder surgery date due 08/25/2026; client employment/commission records due 09/26/2026; reconcile chiro/PT ledgers due 10/05/2026; Advanced Rockland notes/itemized CPT ledger due 10/07/2026; confirm right shoulder arthroscopy date due 10/10/2026; SportsCare ongoing notes due 10/14/2026.

Discovery is stuck on both sides: plaintiff still needs updated maintenance treatment ledgers/notes, and defendants have not produced/accepted scope-of-employment proof, especially vehicle assignment/dispatch records, and Pullano deposition/scope disclosure remains outstanding.

Defendants pleaded comparative negligence, assumption of risk, seatbelt defense, CPLR 4545 collateral source, failure to mitigate, sudden emergency, Public Authorities Law §1276 noncompliance, statute of limitations, and another action pending. Their affirmative-defense BOP also particularizes culpable conduct, seatbelt, failure to mitigate, collateral source, and emergency doctrine.
Index No. 160000/2024. Judge identified in correspondence is Hon. Christopher Chin.
Because chiropractic and PT treatment is ongoing, their ledgers remain open and have not been reconciled line-by-line against CPT codes; SportsCare/Advanced Rockland updated records are still owed.

On 04/29/2024 Claims Service Bureau opened negotiations with an offer well below the $100,000 limit. They disputed liability/mechanism, emphasized clean day-after CT scans, and attacked the wage claim as unsupported by an expert.

No current response is documented. SportsCare produced records through 12/14/2023 in December 2023, but later updated-record requests in 2025–2026 went unanswered per notes/tasks; ongoing notes are still pending.

Client’s current listed residence is in Cypress, Texas, while treatment remains with New York providers such as SportsCare and Advanced Rockland. The file shows he is still attending NY treatment, but the logistics/current address-versus-treatment situation should be clarified.
